title: Labour Party (UK)
wiki_lead:
The Labour Party, commonly Labour, is a political party in the United Kingdom. It sits on the centre-left of the left–right political spectrum, and has historically been an alliance of democratic socialists, social democrats and trade unionists. It has been the governing party since the 2024 general election. Andy Burnham became Leader of the Labour Party and Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in 2026, succeeding Keir Starmer, who had been elected party leader in 2020 and led Labour into government. There have been 12 Labour governments and eight Labour prime ministers. The party meets annually during Autumn for the Labour Party Conference, during which delegates from local parties and trade unions vote on party policy, and senior figures address the audience from the Conference platform. 
The Labour Party was founded in 1900, having emerged from the trade union movement and socialist parties of the 19th century. In 1918 it became guided by socialism and a commitment to "common ownership" via nationalisation. It was electorally weak before the First World War, but in the early 1920s overtook the Liberal Party to become the main opposition to the Conservative Party, and briefly formed a minority government under Ramsay MacDonald in 1924. In 1929 Labour became the largest party in the House of Commons for the first time, with 287 seats, but fell short of a majority, forming another minority government. In 1931, in response to the Great Depression, MacDonald formed a new government with Conservative and Liberal support, which led to his expulsion from the party. Labour was soundly defeated by his coalition in 1931, winning only 52 seats, but began to recover in 1935 with 154 seats.
During the Second World War, Labour served in the wartime coalition, after which it won a majority in 1945 under Clement Attlee. Attlee's government enacted extensive nationalisation and established the modern welfare state and National Health Service before losing power in 1951. Under Harold Wilson and James Callaghan, Labour again governed from 1964 to 1970 and from 1974 to 1979. The party then entered a period of intense internal division, which ended in the defeat of its left wing by the mid-1980s. After electoral defeats to the Conservatives in 1987 and 1992, Tony Blair took the party to the political centre as part of the New Labour rebranding of the party, and it governed under Blair from 1997 to 2007 and Gordon Brown from 2007 to 2010. After several electoral defeats in the 2010s, Starmer moved Labour closer to the political centre after replacing Jeremy Corbyn as its leader in 2020, winning the 2024 general election. On 22 June 2026, Starmer resigned as leader, and was succeeded by Burnham the following month.
The party includes semi-autonomous London, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish branches.

grok_lead: The Labour Party is a centre-left political party in the United Kingdom, formed in 1900 as the Labour Representation Committee by trade unions and socialist groups to advance working-class representation in Parliament, and officially renamed the Labour Party in 1906 after securing 29 seats in that year's general election. It has historically advocated democratic socialism and social democracy, with policies emphasizing state intervention in the economy, workers' rights through union affiliations, and expansion of public services, though its approach evolved toward greater acceptance of market mechanisms under the " New Labour " branding in the 1990s. The party first formed a minority government in 1924 under Ramsay MacDonald, but its most transformative period came after the 1945 landslide victory, when Clement Attlee's administration nationalized key industries, established the National Health Service, and implemented the welfare state framework that defined post-war Britain. Subsequent governments under Harold Wilson and James Callaghan in the 1960s and 1970s pursued modernization, including decimalization and equal pay legislation, but faced economic challenges like inflation and strikes culminating in the 1978â79 Winter of Discontent, contributing to electoral defeat. Under Tony Blair from 1997 to 2010, Labour achieved three consecutive victories, introducing the minimum wage, devolution to Scotland and Wales, and Bank of England independence, though marred by the Iraq War decision and rising public debt. The party suffered defeats in 2010, 2015, and 2019 amid leadership shifts, including Jeremy Corbyn's tenure, which amplified internal divisions over issues like Brexit and antisemitism allegations. Revitalized under Keir Starmer, who became leader in 2020, Labour won a substantial majority in the July 2024 general election, gaining 412 seats with 33.7% of the vote amid widespread dissatisfaction with the prior Conservative government. Starmer resigned in June 2026 amid declining poll ratings, heavy losses in the May 2026 local elections, and internal pressure; Andy Burnham was confirmed as Labour Party leader on 17 July 2026 and became Prime Minister on 20 July 2026.
